skill.name: nuxt4-patterns
skill.description: Use Nuxt 4 patterns to troubleshoot hydration mismatches, fetch page data during server rendering, and choose route-level rendering and lazy loading strategies.
skill.summary: Build and review Nuxt 4 pages with predictable hydration, reusable server-fetched data, and less work on initial load.
skill.author: affaan-m

security_audit.summary: All 38 static alerts were false positives: they matched Markdown formatting, Nuxt data-fetching guidance and a relative API example, or ordinary framework documentation. No evidence of prompt injection, shell execution, or external data transfer was found. A separate finding identifies a blanket API cache rule that could expose personalized responses across users.

remediation.issue: The route rules example caches all API endpoints without distinguishing public responses from authenticated or personalized responses.
remediation.suggestion: Cache only explicitly listed public endpoints whose responses are identical for every user. Leave authenticated and personalized endpoints out of shared caches.

semantic_findings.title: Blanket API Caching Can Expose Private Responses
semantic_findings.description: The example applies a one-hour cache to every route under /api/. If any matching endpoint returns personalized data, shared caching could serve one user's response to another user.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cache rule visibly matches all API routes and does not restrict caching to public responses. The example does not show a private endpoint or an observed disclosure.

content.value_statement: Nuxt pages can render different markup on the server and browser, fetch data twice, or load nonessential components too early. Use Nuxt 4 patterns to diagnose hydration issues, reuse server-fetched data, and choose rendering and loading strategies by route.
actual_capabilities: Identify hydration mismatch risks from browser-only state, nondeterministic values, and URL fragments.
Recommend useFetch or useAsyncData for page reads and explain when to use $fetch for user-triggered actions.
Suggest stable data keys, smaller payloads, and deferred fetching with explicit loading states.
Compare prerendering, stale-while-revalidate, incremental static regeneration, and client rendering for different route groups.
Identify nonessential Vue components that can load conditionally or delay hydration until visible or idle.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples rather than a runnable app or automated test suite.
Does not measure page speed, payload size, or hydration timing.
Incremental static regeneration depends on the deployment platform.
The example cache rule does not account for private API responses and should not be copied as a default.

use_cases.title: Fix a Hydration Warning
use_cases.description: Trace differences between the server HTML and the browser's first render, then isolate the logic that requires the browser.

use_cases.title: Review Page Data Fetching
use_cases.description: Check whether pages reuse server-fetched data during hydration and whether slower secondary requests have clear loading states.

use_cases.title: Plan Rendering by Route
use_cases.description: Choose rendering rules for a homepage, product catalog, and dashboard based on indexing, freshness, and user-specific content.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Hydration Warning
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: A page reads browser storage during its first render.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain why reading browser storage can cause a hydration mismatch. Suggest how to keep the first render consistent before reading the stored value.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Data Composable
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: A page needs required article data and optional comments.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this article page and choose how to load the article and its comments. Explain the data key and show where a pending state belongs.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Component Loading Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: A product page has an interactive gallery and optional recommendations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the component tree and recommend what should load immediately, load conditionally, or hydrate when visible. Explain the tradeoffs for initial interaction.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Route Rendering Policy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: One app serves public pages, a private dashboard, and mixed API endpoints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare rendering options for the provided route groups using indexing and freshness requirements. Identify which public responses can be cached and keep personalized responses out of shared caches.

output_examples.input: The product page shows a hydration warning when it renders a timestamp and reads browser storage.
output: Render the same initial timestamp on the server and client by reusing the server value.
Read browser storage after the component mounts and use a stable placeholder until then.

output_examples.input: An article loads on the server and again on hydration. Comments are not needed for the first render.
output: Load the article through a server-rendered data composable so hydration can reuse the result.
Defer the comments request and show a loading state without blocking navigation.

output_examples.input: The homepage is stable, the catalog changes hourly, and the account dashboard is personalized.
output: Prerender the homepage and consider background revalidation for the public catalog.
Keep personalized dashboard and API responses out of shared caches.

best_practices: Keep the server and client first render consistent, and defer browser-only reads until after mounting.
Use stable data keys and give deferred requests an explicit pending state.
Choose rendering rules per route group and cache only responses that are safe to share.
anti_patterns: Disabling server rendering across the app to hide a hydration mismatch.
Using a direct top-level fetch for page data that the client should reuse from the server.
Applying a shared cache to all API routes without distinguishing public and personalized responses.

faq.question: Which versions of Nuxt does this skill cover?
faq.answer: The guidance targets Nuxt 4. It does not cover migration from older Nuxt versions.

faq.question: When should I use useAsyncData instead of useFetch?
faq.answer: Use useFetch for straightforward API reads. Use useAsyncData when you need a custom data key, a custom fetcher, or multiple async sources.

faq.question: Should I disable server rendering to fix hydration warnings?
faq.answer: First check for differences between the server and client markup. Reserve client-only rendering for areas that genuinely require browser APIs.

faq.question: What is the difference between lazy loading and lazy hydration?
faq.answer: Lazy loading defers the component code download. Lazy hydration defers making server-rendered markup interactive.

faq.question: Does incremental static regeneration work on every host?
faq.answer: No. Check whether your deployment platform supports incremental static regeneration before enabling it.

faq.question: Can I apply the sample API cache rule to every endpoint?
faq.answer: No. Only share cached responses from explicitly public endpoints. Exclude endpoints that return authenticated or user-specific data.
